thesis.name: Nouns Nation Builder Investment Thesis V2
thesis.instrument: SAFE plus sponsor, grant, and cloud-credit stack before any token or DAO financing.
thesis.summary: Nouns Nation Builder is investable as an agent-native media venue first, a Nounish game studio second, and a future onchain community protocol third. V2 adds the venue ladder: browser room, living-room TV, partner venues, and eventually ticketed live finals.

allocation.expansionCeiling: Up to $250k after retention proof, agent-output proof, and one sponsor or ecosystem funding partner.
allocation.operatingRule: Fund the venue, prove the ritual, delay the token.

roadmap.name: Nouns Nation Builder Roadmap V2
roadmap.thesis: Build a web-native arena first, then use agents to operate the broadcast layer, then syndicate the format into TV screens, venues, and eventually ticketed live finals.
roadmap.position: Browser room -> agent-operated broadcast -> TV-ready league -> venue and stadium format.
roadmap.operatingRule: Use AI tools to compress production cost, not to remove human taste. The moat is a repeatable ritual plus machine-readable operations.

pillars.title: What I am buying
pillars.body: A small, fast studio building a Nounish nation: automated leagues, watch-party pages, TV cast surfaces, agent task boards, MCP tools, manifests, recaps, posters, venue kits, and eventually a Builder DAO around the best rituals.

pillars.title: Why it can work
pillars.body: Nouns already proved a strange thing: CC0 art plus auctions plus treasury governance can fund culture. Agents add the missing labor layer. They can scout, explain, QA, remix, and route attention all day.

pillars.title: What must be true
pillars.body: The project must turn passive watching into repeat behavior, prove that agents create useful output rather than noise, and keep the capital stack clean: no disguised security, no extractive token promise.

whyNow.title: Nouns is legible infrastructure
whyNow.body: Nouns.com explains a governance model where Noun holders and delegates fund work through onchain proposals, and Nouns Builder packages nounish DAO creation for new communities.

whyNow.title: Agents are becoming an operating layer
whyNow.body: OpenAI described its April 2026 Agents SDK direction around MCP, skills, shell tools, patch tools, sandbox execution, subagents, and code-mode workflows as normal builder primitives.

whyNow.title: MCP gives agents a doorway
whyNow.body: Anthropic frames MCP as a standard for connecting models to tools and data. Cloudflare now documents remote MCP servers as deployable agent infrastructure.

whyNow.title: PointCast has shipped the shape
whyNow.body: The latest GitHub work is not only content. It is a standalone Nouns Nation hub, Battle Desk V3, Sponsorship Desk, Production Desk, public Claim Board, federation manifest, co-presence, WIRE, FOLLOW, agent visitor centers, media catalogs, agent activity broadcasts, and Nouns Nation agent claim queues.

aiToolingCurve.title: Agent-native production
aiToolingCurve.signal: Agents can inspect repos, run commands, edit files, call MCP tools, and work in sandboxes.
aiToolingCurve.implication: One small team can ship the control room: scorekeeping, highlights, recap drafts, sponsor inventory, QA, and manifests.

aiToolingCurve.title: Distributed media ops
aiToolingCurve.signal: Remote MCP servers, coding agents, and repo-native workflows become normal parts of production.
aiToolingCurve.implication: Partner venues and city nodes can run standardized watch nights while agents keep the desk, feed, and receipts in sync.

aiToolingCurve.title: Physical-world show surface
aiToolingCurve.signal: AI building tools make bespoke media formats cheap enough to rehearse, localize, and package.
aiToolingCurve.implication: The format can graduate from browser league to bar screens, campus nights, festival courts, and a flagship live final.

threeYearRoadmap.title: Prove the weekly ritual
threeYearRoadmap.headline: Make the league room worth returning to every week.
build: Agent desk for scout, host, commentator, QA, and scorekeeper jobs.
Twelve scheduled watch nights with public recap artifacts.
Sponsor kit, season calendar, and clean analytics for repeat viewing.

threeYearRoadmap.title: Syndicate the broadcast network
threeYearRoadmap.headline: Turn one desk into a repeatable local and partner format.
build: A partner kit for bars, campuses, DAO chapters, shops, and clubs.
Federated manifests for local identity, rules, rosters, and results.
A sponsor loop that buys named slates, highlights, and physical nights.
gates: 1,000-plus weekly viewers as a target, not a promise

threeYearRoadmap.title: Package the live final
threeYearRoadmap.headline: Make a browser-native sport legible on a stage or stadium board.
build: A finals format with live host, agent desk, crowd screen, and recap studio.
Venue production runbook for scoreboards, QR handoffs, and sponsor reads.
Licensable season package for community operators.

venueLadder.body: The first venue is the URL: no install, no token prerequisite, readable by humans and agents.
TV cast mode turns the desk into a watch-party surface for AirPlay, HDMI, smart TVs, and club screens.
Partner nodes get a local kit: schedule, QR joins, sponsor reads, results, and manifest handoff.
The final form is an event format: live finals, scoreboard graphics, agent desk, crowd rituals, and ticketed streams.

capitalPlan.label: First check
capitalPlan.body: $50k-$75k for 90 days of product proof: Nouns Nation hub, Battler TV, Agent Bench, Claim Board, Production Desk, scorebook, roadmap deck, sponsor kit, and distribution tests.

capitalPlan.label: Expansion check
capitalPlan.body: Up to $250k after retention proof, agent-output proof, and one sponsor or ecosystem funding partner.

capitalPlan.label: Non-dilutive stack
capitalPlan.body: Pursue OpenAI and Anthropic credits, Nouns or Builder-aligned grants, and protocol ecosystem sponsorship before over-selling equity.

capitalPlan.label: Onchain option
capitalPlan.body: Only launch a Builder DAO after recurring audience behavior exists and counsel has reviewed governance, token, and revenue claims.

capitalGates.unlock: Ninety days of product proof: scheduled watch nights, agent bench loop, analytics, and sponsor collateral.
Released after repeat-viewing proof, useful agent output, and one sponsor or ecosystem funding partner.
Only after partner venues want the format and the production runbook is repeatable without founder heroics.
A Builder DAO or token should follow proven audience behavior, legal review, and clean governance claims.

returnPaths.label: Media
returnPaths.body: Sponsorships, event drops, paid season packages, and branded Nounish broadcasts.

returnPaths.label: Tools
returnPaths.body: Agent-readable publishing kits, MCP endpoints, manifests, QA boards, task queues, and white-label community venues.

returnPaths.label: Protocol
returnPaths.body: A future Nouns Builder DAO with treasury-governed seasons, collectibles, and contributor budgets.

risks.title: Governance risk
risks.body: Nouns auction economics and funding norms can change by vote. Treat Nouns alignment as ecosystem leverage, not guaranteed financing.

risks.title: Retention risk
risks.body: A watch toy must become a ritual. The first hard KPI is repeat viewing across multiple slates, not raw page opens.

risks.title: Agent quality risk
risks.body: Agents can create spam. The moat is prompt design, task scoping, human taste, and a tight artifact loop.

risks.title: Legal risk
risks.body: Do not sell profit expectations through a token. Use counsel before DAO, revenue-share, treasury, or collectible mechanics go live.

risks.title: Security risk
risks.body: MCP and remote tool surfaces need strict permissions, allowlists, rate limits, and audit logs before capital or identities touch them.

diligencePlan.body: Run five watch tests, capture viewer confusion, publish recap artifacts, clean the Battler link circuit, and measure repeat slates.

Recruit agent operators, publish the Agent Bench loop, test scorekeeper and commentator flows, package sponsor inventory, use the Claim Board to route open tasks, and use the Production Desk to reconcile accepted work.
Close one paid sponsor or ecosystem grant, decide whether a Builder DAO is warranted, and only then price a larger round.
